title: Evaluation comparison for a finite free change of ring sheaves
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Suppose that $S$, as an $R$-module sheaf, is isomorphic to $R^{\oplus d}$ for some integer $d\geq0$. Use module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories $D(R),D(S)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the derived change of rings $T=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], derived tensor products $\otimes^{\mathbf L}_R,\otimes^{\mathbf L}_S$ (total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] after K-flat replacement [def-pc-kflat-complex]), and derived internal Hom $H_R,H_S$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], with the derived tensor–Hom adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] and [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] defining transposes. For arbitrary $P,Q\in D(R)$, the canonical morphism
$$c_{P,Q}:T H_R(P,Q)\longrightarrow H_S(TP,TQ)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(S)$, natural contravariantly in $P$ and covariantly in $Q$. It is the tensor-Hom transpose of the pairing
$$TP\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}T H_R(P,Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(P,Q))\xrightarrow{T(\operatorname{ev}_{P,Q})}TQ.$$
In particular this specifies the comparison by evaluation, independently of any choice of the finite free basis. No boundedness, completeness, constructibility or perfectness hypothesis on $P$ or $Q$ is required.

source.place: Tag 08J9, label lemma-internal-hom: derived tensor-Hom adjunction. The finite-free change-of-rings specialization and its evaluation normalization are the auxiliary assertion here, not a verbatim assertion of that tag.

proof.text: Choose an $R$-linear isomorphism $S\cong R^{\oplus d}$ and write $e_j:R\to S$ for its basis inclusions. Let $U$ denote restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For every $X\in D(R)$ there is a natural isomorphism $a_X:X^{\oplus d}\xrightarrow{\sim}UTX$, with components $b_j^X=1_X\otimes e_j$. Indeed, choose a K-flat resolution $F\to X$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and compute $TX$ by $F\otimes_R S$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] gives the degreewise mutually inverse maps $F^{\oplus d}\to U(F\otimes_R S)$, $(x_j)\mapsto\sum_j x_j\otimes e_j$, and $x\otimes\sum_j r_je_j\mapsto(r_jx)_j$; they commute with differentials. Finite sums of the resolution remain quasi-isomorphisms, since kernels and images of a finite block-diagonal differential are the corresponding finite sums. Thus these maps give $a_X$ after localization. This also proves naturality in $X$.

source.place: Tag 08J9, label lemma-internal-hom, and Tag 08JA, label lemma-section-RHom-over-U; agent finite-free specialization using the adjunction counit and finite biproducts.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction] with $K=P$ and $N=TQ$. It gives an isomorphism $\beta:UH_S(TP,TQ)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_R(P,UTQ)$. Its normalization says explicitly that the transpose of $\beta$ is restricted $S$-linear evaluation after inserting the scalar-extension unit $\eta_P:P\to UTP$. The same node states that $U$ reflects isomorphisms. All its hypotheses hold: the site is small and $P,Q$ are arbitrary objects of the ordinary unbounded module-sheaf derived categories. No condensed-coefficient or constructibility hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tag 08J9, label lemma-internal-hom, and Tag 08JA, label lemma-section-RHom-over-U; agent finite-free specialization using the adjunction counit and finite biproducts.

proof.text: Put $H=H_R(P,Q)$. The tensor-Hom adjunction supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] and [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] gives $\operatorname{Hom}(Z,H_R(P,Q^{\oplus d}))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Z,Q^{\oplus d})\cong\prod_j\operatorname{Hom}(P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Z,Q)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Z,H^{\oplus d})$ for every $Z$. The maps are the finite product projections; their inverse assembles the components by the finite biproduct universal property. Hence $H_R(P,Q^{\oplus d})\cong H^{\oplus d}$, with components $H_R(P,\operatorname{pr}_i)$. Composing with $H_R(P,a_Q^{-1})$ gives an isomorphism $\gamma:H_R(P,UTQ)\to H^{\oplus d}$. This is the elementary proof that this particular right adjoint preserves finite products, with finite products equal to finite sums.

source.place: Tag 08J9, label lemma-internal-hom, and Tag 08JA, label lemma-section-RHom-over-U; agent finite-free specialization using the adjunction counit and finite biproducts.

proof.text: Let $c=c_{P,Q}$ be exactly the evaluation transpose in the statement. Compute $\beta\,U(c)\,b_j^H:H\to H_R(P,UTQ)$ by transposing. By the evaluation normalization of [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction], its transpose is $P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_{P,Q}}Q\xrightarrow{b_j^Q}UTQ$: inserting $\eta_P$ inserts the scalar $1_S$, and the defining extended pairing multiplies it by $e_j$, giving $1_Se_j=e_j$. This calculation may be made on the K-flat tensor representatives defining the pairing; it uses only the bilinear tensor relations, so is an equality of the specified morphisms after localization. By uniqueness of transposes, $\beta\,U(c)\,b_j^H=H_R(P,b_j^Q)$. Therefore the $(i,j)$ matrix entry of $\gamma\,\beta\,U(c)\,a_H$ is $H_R(P,\operatorname{pr}_i a_Q^{-1}b_j^Q)=\delta_{ij}1_H$. Maps between finite biproducts are determined by these entries, so this composite is the identity of $H^{\oplus d}$.

source.place: Tag 08J9, label lemma-internal-hom, and Tag 08JA, label lemma-section-RHom-over-U; agent finite-free specialization using the adjunction counit and finite biproducts.

proof.text: The three maps $a_H$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ are isomorphisms, so the identity just computed implies that $U(c)$ is an isomorphism. Conservativity in [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction] implies that $c$ is an isomorphism in $D(S)$. If $d=0$, the same argument takes place between zero biproducts and their unique map is their identity; no positive-rank hypothesis was used. Evaluation and the adjunctions are natural in both arguments, so taking transposes makes $c$ contravariantly natural in $P$ and covariantly natural in $Q$. The original pairing and its unique transpose mention no chosen basis; the basis was used only to test invertibility. This proves the required basis independence and all the asserted clauses for unbounded $P,Q$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q62-db2b5c011 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, all cited node statements, unit sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom, the parent lem-sf-tensor-hom step 8 (which uses the item), the main-20261015 blueprint lem-sf-tensor-hom (the 'compatible with scalar extension' clause), and Stacks sites-cohomology.tex 08JA lemma-section-RHom-over-U and 08J9 lemma-internal-hom (lines 8874-8930). Compared with the base copy, the statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint fields are unchanged; only the proof, status, split_report and appended searches are new. There are no new nodes. The statement is true because S finite free over R is perfect and flat. Tested d=0, d=1, R=k with S=k[eps], and the unbounded case P = direct sum of k[n] (finite free tensor commutes with products). Step 1: the presheaf tensor with R^d is already a sheaf, the explicit inverse maps commute with d, and lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings gives the K-flat computation. Step 2: the hypotheses of lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction hold (small site, commutative rings, no flatness or boundedness needed); it supplies the normalized iso and conservativity of U, and it does not reach the item, so there is no cycle. Step 3: Yoneda with the Hom-adjunction from the internal-Hom node plus rhom-global-sections gives the finite product. Step 4: I re-derived the transpose. It is b_j^{P tensor H}, checkable on K-flat representatives, then by naturality of b_j it becomes b_j^Q composed with ev; the matrix entries are delta_ij. This is the specified evaluation morphism, not just some isomorphism. Step 5: conservativity, the d=0 case and basis independence are correct. Duplicate candidates checked and rejected: lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension (narrower, completed integral bounded), lem-sf-hom-comparison-finite-free (a different functor), lem-pur-ringed-site-finite-free-dual-pullback, lem-sf-hom-finite-projective, lem-pod-finite-projective-tensor-hom. No SGA. All seven declared tool_uses accepted as generic black-box ringed-site tools. Mathlib searches cover all three kinds (one leansearch recorded honestly as unavailable). No fixes.
